## Audit note (epic 3405-c0b7) — refined-bar guidance may resolve this deferred/latent decision

Under the sharpened standard (prefer an existing broad-but-accurate code; reserve new vocabulary for demonstrated need): the editor missing-bundle `WorkflowError` (a `WorkflowParseError`) is not a provider-availability condition, so `llm_unavailable` mis-fits it. The honest existing-vocab fit is **`command_failed`** — "an unclassified rebar command failure" accurately covers "could not load the workflow bundle" without claiming an outage.

The single root change (narrow `error_code_for` branch 6 so `llm_unavailable` fires only for `LLMUnavailableError`) fixes this too, with no new vocabulary. Note also that the SAME `WorkflowParseError` class is now shown OBSERVABLE via the `render_workflow` MCP read tool (child 7d47) — so this is no longer purely CLI-only/latent; the branch emits the misleading code on a live MCP surface today. Suggest this may be downgradable from escalate to ready-to-fix (target `command_failed`); flagging for the owner rather than transitioning it (read-only audit).
